Fact.Name: Virginia cities and counties
Fact.Description: The 133 localities in the 2024 Form 760 instructions' list, as option values.

Fact.Name: City or county the filer lived in on January 1, 2025
Fact.Description: Form 760 header, "Locality Code"; 2024 instructions page 14: "the locality in which you lived on January 1, 2025 ... Local school funding is allocated based in part on this information." Asked and confirmed by the filer: the federal address gives a city name and a ZIP, but a ZIP can straddle localities and the date is the day after the tax year. When the ZIP lies in one locality, website-static/js/virginia-locality.js fills this in from it, and the filer confirms it.

Form 760 locality code
Fact.Description: The 3-digit code for /vaLocality, from the list beginning on page 45 of the 2024 Form 760 instructions. One case per locality and no default: a locality missing from this list leaves the code incomplete rather than blank, and scripts/check-virginia-constants.py fails if any option of /vaLocalityOptions is missing here or in /vaUseTaxRate.

Fact.Name: Consumer's use tax rate where the filer lives
Fact.Description: 2024 Form 760 instructions, Line 33, "Tax Rates": 5.3% general (4.3% state + 1% local); 6% in the Northern Virginia, Hampton Roads and Central Virginia regions (+0.7% regional); 6.3% in the localities with the additional 1% local option; 7% in the Historic Triangle. Richmond City is in the Central Virginia region. Every locality is listed in exactly one tier, the 5.3% tier included, and there is no default: an unlisted locality leaves the rate incomplete rather than silently 5.3%; scripts/check-virginia-constants.py enforces the listing.
